project: Namias Portfolio v1 - SSR Performance Finish
summary: Finish the streaming SSR architecture by optimizing critical resources (fonts, images, CSS, JS loading) so the portfolio delivers sub-second FCP and LCP even on slow 3G / mobile data. The core streaming architecture is already implemented — this PRD adds the final optimization layer.
narrative: The homepage already uses streaming SSR with per-section Suspense boundaries, but several critical-path optimizations are still missing: (1) fonts use display:'swap' which causes FOIT on slow connections, (2) the hero image lacks explicit fetch priority, (3) non-critical scripts (analytics, Lenis, service worker) load during initial render, (4) no resource hints for Sanity CDN preconnect or image preload, (5) no critical CSS inlining. These gaps mean slow-connection visitors still see a flash of invisible text and wait for scripts they don't need to see the hero. This PRD closes each gap with minimal, independently-verifiable slices.
principles: No visual changes — the site must look identical after optimization
One optimization per commit — each slice is independently verifiable
Backward compatible — feature flag IS_STREAMING_SSR_ENABLED stays on
Measure before and after — Lighthouse on simulated 3G is the benchmark
Zero regressions — all 498 tests must pass, react-doctor score stays >= 55

personas.label: Visitor on mobile data / slow 3G
goals: See hero text and image within 2 seconds

personas.label: Visitor on broadband
painPointsToday: Marginal delays from unoptimized resource loading

done: HomeContentStreaming with Suspense boundaries for all 9 sections
11 per-section server data fetchers (hero, about, tech-stack, projects, experience, connect, blog, certifications, gallery, site-settings, seo)
SectionProvider for backward compatibility with existing client components
missing: Hero profile image lacks priority={true} and fetchPriority='high'
Inter font uses display: 'swap' (causes FOIT on slow connections)
Umami analytics loads during initial render via layout.tsx
Lenis smooth scroll initializes on mount (blocks interaction)
No performance measurement endpoint for streaming metrics
OpenNext Cloudflare cache headers not configured for streaming HTML

targetArchitecture.overview: Streaming SSR with optimized critical path — fonts, images, scripts, and CSS are loaded in priority order so above-the-fold content paints as fast as possible.
loadingWaterfall: 1. Server sends HTML shell + critical CSS inline + preconnect/preload hints
2. Browser paints hero skeleton immediately (no JS needed)
3. Font loads with display: 'optional' — text appears after 100ms or with fallback font
4. Hero profile image loads with priority + fetchPriority high
5. Hero section data arrives from Sanity (~200ms), stream replaces skeleton
6. Below-the-fold sections stream in as their queries resolve
7. Umami analytics loads after interactive (strategy: afterInteractive)
8. Service worker registers after load (strategy: lazyOnload)
9. Lenis initializes on first user interaction or idle callback

primary: Zero CLS from font swap (FOIT eliminated)
secondary: No hydration warnings in browser console

nonGoals: Rewrite any section component (they already work)
Change the visual design or layout
Change Sanity schema or data fetching logic

designDecisions.choice: Use display: 'optional' for Inter font. This gives the browser 100ms to load the font before falling back to a system font. On slow connections, text paints immediately with the fallback, then swaps when the font arrives.
designDecisions.rationale: display: 'swap' causes a flash of invisible text (FOIT) for up to 3 seconds on slow connections. display: 'optional' eliminates FOIT entirely at the cost of the font maybe not loading on the first visit. Since the font is cached on subsequent visits, this is the right tradeoff.
alternativesConsidered: display: 'swap' + font preload (rejected: still blocks text paint on slow connections)
Use a system font stack (rejected: loses brand identity)

designDecisions.choice: Next.js <Script> component with strategy='afterInteractive' for analytics and strategy='lazyOnload' for service worker and Lenis.
designDecisions.rationale: prevents third-party scripts from blocking the initial render. afterInteractive loads after hydration, lazyOnload loads when the browser is idle.
alternativesConsidered: Dynamic imports with useEffect (rejected: more complex, no built-in priority)

designDecisions.choice: Inline the most critical CSS rules (hero layout, typography, colors) directly in layout.tsx as a <style> tag. This is a one-time manual extraction of ~20 rules versus a full toolchain.
designDecisions.rationale: Full critical CSS extraction (critters, penthouse) adds tooling complexity for diminishing returns on a portfolio site. Manual inline of the ~20 rules that control above-the-fold rendering is simpler and faster to implement.
alternativesConsidered: critters npm package (rejected: adds build complexity)
No critical CSS (rejected: render-blocking stylesheet request hurts FCP)

epics.title: Critical resource optimization
epics.summary: Optimize fonts, hero image, and critical CSS so above-the-fold content paints as fast as possible.

stories.title: Change font display from swap to optional
stories.details: Change Inter font from display: 'swap' to display: 'optional' in layout.tsx. Add a system font fallback in the CSS variable chain.

stories.title: Add priority + fetchPriority to hero image
stories.details: Ensure the hero profile image has priority={true} and fetchPriority='high'. This tells the browser to load it before other images.

stories.title: Add preconnect hint for Sanity CDN
stories.details: Add <link rel='preconnect' href='https://cdn.sanity.io'> in layout.tsx <head> to warm up the connection before section data fetches.

stories.title: Add preload for hero profile image
stories.details: Add <link rel='preload' as='image' href='...'> for the hero profile image URL in layout.tsx <head>. Fetch the URL from fetchHeroData() or use a static default.

stories.title: Inline critical CSS for above-the-fold content
stories.details: Extract the CSS rules that control hero section layout (container, card, typography, accent colors) and inline them as a <style> tag in layout.tsx.

epics.title: Script loading optimization
epics.summary: Defer non-critical scripts (analytics, service worker, Lenis) so they don't block the initial paint or hydration.

stories.title: Move Umami analytics to afterInteractive
stories.details: Change the Analytics component to use next/script with strategy='afterInteractive'. This loads the analytics script after the page is interactive.

stories.title: Move service worker registration to lazyOnload
stories.details: Change service worker registration to use next/script with strategy='lazyOnload' or register in a useEffect with requestIdleCallback.

stories.title: Defer Lenis initialization
stories.details: Initialize Lenis smooth scroll after the page is interactive. Use a useEffect with requestIdleCallback or IntersectionObserver so it doesn't block first paint.

epics.title: Performance instrumentation
epics.summary: Add performance monitoring to measure and track streaming SSR improvements.

stories.title: Add Server-Timing headers for section fetches
stories.details: Add Server-Timing header that reports per-section fetch durations. This allows measuring streaming performance from the browser Network tab.

stories.title: Create performance test for TTFB and HTML shell size
stories.details: Write a vitest test that fetches the homepage (via Route Handler or test server) and asserts TTFB < 1000ms and initial HTML shell < 20KB.

stories.title: Run full verification suite
stories.details: Run npm run tsc --noEmit, npm run lint, npm run test -- --run, and npm run doctor:check. All must pass.

stories.title: Commit all changes
stories.details: Commit each story as an independent slice with descriptive messages.
